__comment: Generated by `npm run smoke-baseline:update`. Components known to fail the real-render smoke sweep. Shrink this list; do not grow it. See tests/smoke/renderAll.smoke.spec.js.
__notesAreHandWritten: `knownFailing` is regenerated from a real run; `notes` is hand-written and preserved across regeneration. Add a note whenever you add an entry — say whether it is a component defect or a limit of the sweep, and where the fix belongs.

knownFailing.CnAppRoot: threw: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'toString')
knownFailing.CnNotificationPreferences: threw: Cannot destructure property 'registerSection' of '(0 , _useAppSettingsDialogC73Wx6iQ.u)(...)' as it is undefined.

notes.CnAppRoot: LIMIT OF THE SWEEP, not a defect. CnAppRoot drives the whole app shell: it reads capabilities, resolves a manifest through async phases, and expects a router. Its seven dedicated specs each build that harness explicitly (five of them mock @nextcloud/capabilities per file). A generic minimal-prop mount cannot stand it up, and making the sweep do so would mean encoding one component's whole environment into a lane that is supposed to be uniform. Coverage lives in tests/components/CnAppRoot*.spec.js.
notes.CnNotificationPreferences: LIMIT OF THE SWEEP, not a defect. The component calls @nextcloud/vue's `useAppSettingsDialog()`, which reads a provide() supplied by an NcAppSettingsDialog ancestor and returns undefined without one, so destructuring `registerSection` throws. It is only ever mounted inside that dialog in real use. A per-component spec that wraps it correctly is the right home for its coverage.
